description:
05-09 (CPF4131 / TXMIGR TO(2)) end-to-end rehearsal, CONNECTION A of two (A=this directory, B=verify/part05-txmigr-to2b - see that manifest's own description for why the split exists and what it runs). REVISION 2 (2026-09-27): the original single-connection design was rewritten after two reviewers found it violated this harness's own hang-risk-last rule twice (RJU0900B sat mid-array, RJU0900A sat second-to-last) and that its one OBJECT_STATISTICS collect step could not by itself prove 'JUCHUL1's OBJCREATED is unchanged across the connection' (a single snapshot has nothing to diff against). Both findings are fixed by splitting what was one connection into two REAL SSH connections (two manifests/batch directories), which resolves a THIRD problem the first reviewer also raised (not just a rule violation but a genuine risk): JU0900C shares JUCHUD's OPNQRYF-built ODP with ZA0500 (OVRDBF SHARE(*YES)), RJU0900B's ZA0500 sub-call is expected to crash mid-cycle with RPG0907 before its own LR/close, and whether that ODP is actually released before a LATER OPNQRYF in the SAME job was an open question - ending this connection's own job (and thus tearing down anything it opened) before connection B's OPNQRYF ever runs removes that risk structurally instead of arguing it away.

WHAT THIS CONNECTION (A) DOES: builds the DBVER=1 sample DB fresh in &LIB2 (TXSETUP's own PARM(&LIB &CLONEDIR &FORCE) header confirms LIB is an ordinary caller-supplied parameter, default *CURLIB - so TXSETUP LIB(&LIB2) FORCE(*YES) builds the whole DBVER=1 sample DB directly in &LIB2, <USER>B, leaving &LIB, <USER>2, as the tool-hosting library and never touching <USER>1), compiles JU0900C/ZA0500/JU0300 into &LIB2 while JUCHUM/JUCHUL1 are still in their ORIGINAL (pre-JUDLV) shape - so every one of these programs bakes in the OLD record format level ID - then applies the manual CHGPF (05-09's own walkthrough steps 1-4, and the same thing tools/qclsrc/txmigr.clp's own 'Step 1' does) via src/runchgpf.clp, and finally CALLs JU0900C once (RJU0900B, the literal last step) to see whether that stale level ID actually produces the CPF4131 05-09 predicts. TXMIGR TO(2) itself - the tool this whole exercise is nominally about testing - is NOT called anywhere in this connection; that is connection B's job, run against the &LIB2 state THIS connection leaves behind (same DEPENDENCY connection B's own description states explicitly, so run B only after A has actually completed, and only if A's own VFYLOG shows RUNCHGPF finishing without 'CHGPF failed').

NEW IN THIS REVISION - RUNPROBE (src/runprobe.clp, reviewer 2's 'lesson-claim-verification' finding): JU0900C's own MONMSG(CPF0000) on its RCVF of JUCHUM sends a generic 'JU0900C: could not read JUCHUM.' message and falls through to CALL ZA0500 regardless (see ju0900c.clp's own header) - so RJU0900B alone cannot tell a real CPF4131 apart from ZA0500's already-known RPG0907 (05-13 ticket 1's still-unfixed MINQTY 3,0/5,0 mismatch, confirmed reliable by part05-ju0900c-baseline), and verify/lib/clgen.mjs's own insertLog only saves SUBST(MESSAGE_TEXT,1,200), not MESSAGE_ID, so VFYLOG cannot disambiguate by ID either. RUNPROBE is a small, RPG-free CL program (DCLF FILE(JUCHUM) + OVRDBF + RCVF only, structurally identical to JU0900C's own JUCHUM-reading half but never CALLing ZA0500 or touching JUCHUD at all) with a staged MONMSG chain (CPF4131 first, then CPF0864, then a generic CPF0000 catch-all, each SNDPGMMSG-ing an unambiguous, distinctly-worded marker) so VFYLOG can show CPF4131 unambiguously by TEXT even without an ID column. RUNPROBE's SOURCE and compiled *PGM both live in &LIB2 (not &LIB), specifically so that TXMIGR's own Step 3 in connection B ('recompile EVERY *PGM object in the library', tools/qclsrc/txmigr.clp) sweeps it up automatically alongside JU0900C/ZA0500/JU0300 - see that file's own header comment for why this placement is load-bearing, not incidental. It is compiled here (CPRUNPROBE), in this same connection, against the OLD JUCHUM format (before RUNCHGPF), then called once as PROBEB, right after RUNCHGPF - expected to show 'CPF4131 CONFIRMED'. It is safe to place PROBEB mid-array (not last): it never CALLs any RPG program, so its only plausible escapes (CPF4131, CPF0864, or an unmonitored CPF0000) are ordinary *ESCAPE-class messages a 'cl' step's own MONMSG already catches, never an *INQUIRY-class message - CHGJOB INQMSGRPY(*DFT) (auto-inserted at the top of every wrapper) is a fallback this step should never actually need.

NEW IN THIS REVISION - DSPFD *RCDFMT snapshots (reviewer 2's finding that the lesson's core technical object, the record format itself, was never directly observed at any stage): SNAP0JM/SNAP0JL capture JUCHUM's and JUCHUL1's field lists (DSPFD TYPE(*RCDFMT) OUTPUT(*OUTFILE)) BEFORE RUNCHGPF touches anything - the true pre-change baseline (expect no JUDLV field in either). SNAP1JM re-captures JUCHUM immediately after RUNCHGPF (expect its row to differ from SNAP0JM's) - direct structural proof CHGPF actually changed JUCHUM's shape, independent of any message text. SNAP1JL ALSO re-captures JUCHUL1 immediately after RUNCHGPF, into a NEW outfile (FDJL0B, distinct from SNAP0JL's own FDJL0) - added after advisor review, 2026-09-27, which flagged that skipping this second JUCHUL1 snapshot would silently assume the very thing this design is supposed to test: db/v1/juchul1.lf is `R JUCHUR PFILE(JUCHUM)` with NO field list of its own (a shared-format LF, confirmed by reading that DDS source directly), so whether CHGPF-ing the underlying JUCHUM ALSO changes what JUCHUL1 itself reports (without JUCHUL1 ever being recreated) is exactly the kind of thing that must be observed, not assumed - src/runchgpf.clp only ever issues CHGPF against JUCHUM, never touches JUCHUL1 directly, but 'never touched directly' is not the same claim as 'unaffected', and this repo has no primary-source statement settling it either way. If SNAP1JL's row is identical to SNAP0JL's, CHGPF's effect stayed confined to JUCHUM as assumed, and whatever change SNAP2JL (connection B, right after TXMIGR) shows can be attributed to TXMIGR's own Step 2 (or connection B's own manual fix) alone. If SNAP1JL already differs from SNAP0JL, that assumption was wrong, and SNAP2JL's own reading in connection B needs to be revisited against THIS baseline (FDJL0B), not FDJL0. DSPFD's own OUTFILE record layout is NOT confirmed against any primary source in this repo (work/design/refs/cl_commands_75.txt has no DSPFD entry at all, same gap already noted for DCLF/RCVF/CHGPF; a targeted grep of every file under work/design/refs/ for QAFDRFMT/DSPFFD/'format level' found nothing that pins down TYPE(*RCDFMT)'s own outfile columns specifically) - TYPE(*RCDFMT)/OUTPUT(*OUTFILE) themselves are long-standing, extremely common IBM i CL usage (same category of confidence this repo already extended to DCLF's OPNID()), but the exact outfile columns, and in particular whether *RCDFMT's outfile even lists field NAMES at all (as opposed to one summary row per format - record length, field count, and similar - with field names belonging to a different DSPFFD-style output instead) are not confirmed, so every corresponding collect step below reads 'SELECT *' rather than named columns, and expected/notes.md's own reading guide does NOT rely solely on spotting the literal text 'JUDLV' - it also reads whatever record-length/field-count-shaped columns actually come back, comparing them row-to-row across snapshots, which works regardless of which columns *RCDFMT actually returns.

OBJECT_STATISTICS collect step - CORRECTED CLAIM (reviewer 1's finding that the original description's 'an unchanged JUCHUL1 OBJCREATED timestamp... would itself prove TXMIGR's CRTLF never actually recreated it' cannot hold from a single snapshot): this connection's own collect step is now framed only as a BASELINE data point (JUCHUM/JUCHUL1/JU0300/JU0900C/ZA0500/RUNPROBE's OBJCREATED as of the end of connection A, before TXMIGR has ever run) to diff against connection B's own final OBJECT_STATISTICS collect - not as proof of anything by itself. See verify/part05-txmigr-to2b/expected/notes.md for the corrected reading (advisor review, 2026-09-27, also flagged that even the two-snapshot comparison is complicated by connection B's own manual DLTF/CRTLF step, which changes JUCHUL1's OBJCREATED regardless of what TXMIGR itself did - SNAP1JM/SNAP2JL/SNAP3JL's structural field-list evidence is the more reliable signal for 'did TXMIGR's own CRTLF work', not OBJCREATED).

Everything below UNCHANGED from the original single-connection design (still applies verbatim): CLONEDIR handling, the CCSID-1208-conversion dance for db/v1/*.pf, db/v1/*.lf and db/v2/juchum.pf (heredoc'd files are tagged CCSID 273/EBCDIC by this harness's own confirmed default, verify/README.md; TXSETUP's own LOADPF/LOADLF and RUNCHGPF's own CPYFRMSTMF hardcode STMFCCSID(1208), so each DDS source is uploaded as an ordinary throwaway-named member - JUCHUMV1/JUCHUMV2/etc - then converted to a genuine CCSID-1208 IFS file via a 'sh' step's CPYTOSTMF, mirroring verify/part05-txlegacy-exec), TXSETUP/RUNCHGPF being invoked via QCMDEXC through tiny dedicated helper CL programs (src/runsetup.clp, src/runchgpf.clp) rather than a literal 'TXSETUP LIB(...)' statement embedded in a step's own cmd text (the CL compiler resolves a *CMD's syntax at COMPILE time, but TXSETUP's own *CMD is only created by an earlier step's RUNTIME action inside this SAME wrapper job - the exact problem and fix verify/part05-txlegacy-exec/src/txlegrun.clp's own header comment already documents for TXLEGACY), JU0900C/ZA0500/JU0300 being placed as plain IFS files (no remoteSrcFile/member - that option has no &LIB2 form) and copied into &LIB2/QCLSRC/QRPGSRC (freshly CRTSRCPF'd there, RCDLEN(92)) by 'sh' steps doing a plain CPYFRMSTMF with no CCSID override, the explicit ADDLIBLE LIB(&LIB2) POSITION(*FIRST) that stays in effect for every later 'cl' step in this same connection (JU0900C's unqualified DCLF FILE(JUCHUM), JU0300's unqualified FJUCHUL1 F-spec, and now RUNPROBE's own unqualified DCLF FILE(JUCHUM) all need &LIB2 on the *LIBL at COMPILE time), and JU0900C being called with RUNMODE='*TEST' (matching part05-ju0900c-baseline's own CONFIRMED SUCCESS, so ZA0500's own MONMSG-guarded UPDAT never fires and no TXRESET is needed afterward).

REVISION 3 (2026-09-27, second advisor review after Revision 2 above): (1) PRECLEAN (DLTF FILE(&LIB2/JUCHUL1) then DLTF FILE(&LIB2/JUCHUM), both MONMSG CPF0000, right before RUNSETUP) was added because tools/qclsrc/txsetup.clp's own LOADPF/LOADLF subroutines only CRTPF/CRTLF a table 'if it is not there yet' (their own header comment: 'Do not overwrite a file the learner may already have built by hand... Only create it if it is not there yet') - RUNSETUP's own FORCE(*YES) only controls whether TXSETUP proceeds past its own early-exit check, NOT whether LOADPF/LOADLF's own per-object CHKOBJ-then-conditional-CRTPF/CRTLF logic recreates an object that already exists. Without PRECLEAN, a RETRY of this same connection against a &LIB2 that already has SOME state from a prior partial run (or a &LIB2 that was not actually the pristine empty library docs/probes.md's P01 describes) could leave JUCHUM/JUCHUL1 in whatever shape they already were - possibly already in the v2/JUDLV shape - defeating this whole connection's central premise (that JU0900C/ZA0500/JU0300/RUNPROBE are compiled here against the OLD format). PRECLEAN makes this connection idempotent against its own retries: on a genuinely fresh &LIB2 (the expected case, matching P01) both DLTFs simply fail harmlessly (CPF2105/object not found, caught by MONMSG CPF0000) and cost nothing. (2) CLNFDJA/CLNFDJB (DLTF of each DSPFD outfile - FDJM0/FDJL0 and FDJM1/FDJL0B respectively - right before each pair of DSPFD calls) were added so this connection does not depend on DSPFD OUTPUT(*OUTFILE)'s own OUTMBR default (*FIRST, with an ADD-vs-REPLACE choice this repo's own WebFetch below could not pin down with full certainty) - deleting each outfile first guarantees DSPFD creates it fresh every time, regardless of that default, the same DLTF-then-recreate idiom already used throughout this connection for JUCHUL1 itself. (3) DSPFD's own syntax was checked this session via WebFetch (ibm.com/docs/api/v1/content/ssw_ibm_i_75/cl/dspfd.htm, 2026-09-27, per this session's own 'do not guess new CL syntax that could fail the whole wrapper's COMPILE, not just one step's runtime' rule - matching verify/part05-promote-rollback's own precedent for CRTSAVF/SAVOBJ/etc): TYPE(*RCDFMT) is confirmed valid ('The record format names and record format level information for the specified file are provided'), and OUTPUT(*OUTFILE) with TYPE(*RCDFMT) resolves to the real, IBM-documented outfile model OUTFILE=QAFDRFMT/FORMAT=QWHFDFMT - this is a genuine, existing model file, not a guess. The exact QWHFDFMT column list itself (whether it carries a literal level-identifier field, per-field names, or only per-format summary counts) could NOT be confirmed via WebFetch in this session (the fetched pages describe the command's own parameters, not QWHFDFMT's field layout) - this is why every DSPFD-derived collect step still reads 'SELECT *' and expected/notes.md's own reading guide does not assume any particular column name, only that a before/after row comparison works regardless of which columns come back. (4) Both notes.md files (this connection's and connection B's) now instruct the reader to confirm 'TXSETUP: done. DBVER=1.' (this connection, a LITERAL string in txsetup.clp's own SNDPGMMSG - no variable substitution, no zero-padding) actually appears in VFYLOG before trusting any SNAP*/PROBE* reading - advisor review pointed out that TXSETUP's own FAILSAFE label sends a MSGTYPE(*COMP) message and returns NORMALLY (not an *ESCAPE), so RUNSETUP's own step-level MONMSG would never show 'FAILED' even if TXSETUP itself stopped partway through - a silent partial failure inside TXSETUP would otherwise look identical to a real result. (See connection B's own description for the equivalent TXMIGR gate, and why its gate string is 'TXMIGR: done.' rather than a literal 'DBVER=2.' - that message DOES go through a *DEC-to-*CHAR CHGVAR, unlike TXSETUP's.)

REVISION 4 (2026-09-27, third advisor review): a SEPARATE bug was found and fixed in tools/qclsrc/txmigr.clp itself (outside this manifest, but load-bearing for connection B, which actually compiles and calls TXMIGR): the OPNID() fix from Revision 2/3's own static review (OPNID(TXMDBR)/OPNID(TXMPGM) on the two DCLF statements) had NOT also renamed the field references used everywhere below (&WHRELI/&WHREFI/&ODOBNM/&ODOBAT) to match - WebFetch of ibm.com/docs/api/v1/content/ssw_ibm_i_75/cl/dclf.htm confirmed OPNID(value) RENAMES every DCLF-generated field variable to &value_fieldname, so once OPNID(TXMDBR)/OPNID(TXMPGM) took effect, the OLD unqualified names became simply undeclared - this alone would have failed CPTXMIGRRW/CPTXMIGR (connection B's own compile steps) outright on undeclared-variable errors, independent of any length question. Fixed by renaming every reference to the properly-prefixed form, using single-letter OPNID(D)/OPNID(P) (unrelated to the FILE(QTEMP/TXMDBR)/FILE(QTEMP/TXMPGM) qualifiers, which are untouched) rather than OPNID(TXMDBR)/OPNID(TXMPGM) - giving &D_WHRELI/&D_WHREFI/&P_ODOBNM/&P_ODOBAT (8 characters after &). A separate, genuinely UNRESOLVED question (not asserted either way, see that file's own updated header comment) is whether a longer OPNID-generated name like &TXMDBR_WHRELI would even have been legal on length grounds at all - a WebSearch-cited general rule suggests CL variable names cap at 11 characters including &, but the very same dclf.htm page's own example ('&FILE1_CUSTNAME', 14 characters after &) contradicts a flat reading of that cap applying to OPNID-generated names, so this repo does not claim to know which reading is correct. The short D/P prefix was kept anyway as the conservative choice that is legal under either reading, at no cost.

Coordination note (unchanged, still relevant): verify/part05-promote-rollback/manifest.json also targets library2:"*B" and is independent of this pair of manifests (it only ever touches TK0100D/TK0100/TXPRSAVF in &LIB2, never JUCHUM/JUCHUL1/JU0300/JU0900C/ZA0500/RUNPROBE) - but if it runs BETWEEN this connection and connection B, its own TK0100/TK0100D objects would also sit in &LIB2 by the time connection B's TXMIGR call does its own blanket 'recompile every *PGM in &LIB2' pass; TXMIGR would attempt (and, per its own MONMSG, harmlessly fail) to recompile them too, since their source members live only in &LIB's QRPGSRC/QDDSSRC, not &LIB2's - adding a few unrelated 'TXMIGR: could not recompile TK0100 (RPG).'-style lines to VFYLOG but not corrupting anything. Objects are deliberately left in &LIB2 after this connection (no TXRESET/cleanup step): &LIB2 (<USER>B) is the SAVF/scratch role, not a learner-facing library, and connection B depends on finding this connection's own JU0900C/ZA0500/JU0300/RUNPROBE/JUCHUM(post-CHGPF)/JUCHUL1(pre-CHGPF) state intact.

steps.label: ENSCLSRC2
steps.cmd: system "CRTSRCPF FILE(&LIB2/QCLSRC) RCDLEN(92) TEXT('Curriculum CL sources')" 2>&1

steps.label: ENSRPGSRC2
steps.cmd: system "CRTSRCPF FILE(&LIB2/QRPGSRC) RCDLEN(92) TEXT('Curriculum RPG sources')" 2>&1

steps.label: PRECLEAN
steps.cmd:
DLTF FILE(&LIB2/JUCHUL1)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
DLTF FILE(&LIB2/JUCHUM)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)

steps.label: CLNFDJA
steps.cmd:
DLTF FILE(&LIB2/FDJM0)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
DLTF FILE(&LIB2/FDJL0)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)

steps.label: CLNFDJB
steps.cmd:
DLTF FILE(&LIB2/FDJM1)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
DLTF FILE(&LIB2/FDJL0B)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)

steps.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS N, MIN(JUDLV) AS MINDLV FROM &LIB2/JUCHUM
SELECT OBJNAME, OBJTYPE, OBJCREATED FROM TABLE(QSYS2.OBJECT_STATISTICS('&LIB2', '*ALL')) X WHERE OBJNAME IN ('JUCHUM', 'JUCHUL1', 'JU0300', 'JU0900C', 'ZA0500', 'RUNPROBE') ORDER BY OBJNAME
